newsitem.title: USA: Applied Magnetics tumbles on revs view cut.
newsitem.headline: Applied Magnetics tumbles on revs view cut.

text.p: Shares of Applied Magnetics Corp tumbled sharply in unusually busy trade Thursday, activity sparked by Montgomery Securities cutting its fiscal 1997 revenue estimate for the maker of computer disk drive heads, according to market sources.

Applied finished the New York Stock Exchange regular session with a 4-7/8 fall to 33-3/8, a market decline of 12.75 percent. The almost 2.5 million shares traded nearly doubled the stock's average daily volume.
Paul Fox, the analyst who cut the revenue forecast, cited the change for Applied's sharp decline.
Traders agreed the sell-off was inspired by the Montgomery move.
Fox told Reuters he cut the revenue forecast for the year ending in September to $577 million from $616 million because Applied is experiencing a shortage of disk-drive head stacks.
He said his buy recommendation remains unchanged and he made no reduction in earnings estimates.
Applied, he said, is forecast to earn $3.79 in the current fiscal year and $5.70 in fiscal 1998 next year.
Thursday's sharp move extended a substantial decline in the stock that began with Applied's February 24 announcement of a hostile takeover bid for Read-Rite Corp.
When it was announced, the offer to swap 0.679 Applied shares for each Read-Rite share was worth $1.8 billion.
But that total was calculated on an Applied share price of $55.25 as of the February 21 market close.
The three-week tumble has wiped out a spectacular rise in Applied shares over the first six weeks of 1997.
Applied's price peaked with an intraday high of 60-1/2 on February 19, double the price at the beginning of the year.
Meanwhile, Read-Rite's shares have given back some of the sharp rise to an intraday high of 36-1/4 hit February 25.
On Thursday, the shares shed 1/4 to close at 29-3/4.
Read-Rite, also a maker of disk drive components said a combination with Applied would interfere with its strategy for the future, and has turned down the bid.
